title: Krabi Town Cafe Itinerary: 2 Days of Cafes & Riverside | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A no-island Krabi plan focused on Krabi Town cafes, the Friday–Sunday evening Walking Street, and a longtail boat to Khao Khanab Nam. Laid out day by day so you can follow it for real.
keywords: Krabi Town things to do, Krabi cafes, Krabi Walking Street, Khao Khanab Nam, Krabi itinerary
h1:
Krabi Town & Cafe Plan
Cafes · Walking Street · Khao Khanab Nam
intro: Not everyone who comes to Krabi wants to board a boat for the islands at dawn. Some people would rather sleep in, settle into a chilled-out cafe, wander the old town, and end the day at the Walking Street with views of Khao Khanab Nam along the Krabi River. This plan does exactly that — two full days centered on Krabi Town, with short walks and short rides, no battling the wind and waves at sea.

blocks.html: Krabi Town is smaller than many people expect. Walking from Chao Fah Pier to the Maharaj Road area takes under 15 minutes. The good cafes cluster around Maharaj Road and its side sois, while the evening food and market atmosphere happens at the Walking Street, which only opens on Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings. If you're coming for a town-focused trip like this, plan your visit to overlap a weekend so you catch the Walking Street.

items: People who aren't into sea activities — prone to motion or seasickness, or just want a break from harsh sun
Cafe and photo lovers — Krabi has plenty of new in-town cafes, nicely decorated, good for working too
People short on time — land in the afternoon, or fly out the next morning, and you can still do the town properly
Families with older travelers — short walks, easy rest stops, no climbing into boats to reach islands

blocks.title: Timing the key day
blocks.html: Krabi Walking Street only opens Friday–Saturday–Sunday evenings (roughly 5:00–10:00 PM). Come on a weekday and you'll miss it. Line up your Walking Street night with a day you're in town. Khao Khanab Nam, on the other hand, works any day.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old-town cafes, ending with Khao Khanab Nam in the evening

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Sleep in, walk the town, sit in a cafe, finish by the river

items.note: A minimalist wood-toned cafe known for its house-baked croissants and homemade bakery, with vegan options too. Coffee and bakery runs about THB 120–200 per person. There's a hostel upstairs — quiet and comfortable to linger.

items.activity: Stroll the Maharaj Road area and old town
items.note: Look at the old shophouses, souvenir shops, and the black-crab statue at the roundabout — the town's symbol. Easy photo walking, all close together.
Southern-style curry-rice shops around Maharaj Road are cheap, about THB 50–70 a plate, with bold, properly Southern flavors. Tell them if you don't want it spicy.

items.activity: Cafe time to work or escape the heat at Urban café x workspace (K-Avenue, Maharaj Road)
items.note: A two-floor loft cafe in black tones with good coffee, open 8:00 AM–6:00 PM, with power outlets so you can work. Plenty of drinks and cakes to choose from.

items.activity: Longtail boat to Khao Khanab Nam from Chao Fah Pier
items.note: A round-trip charter runs about THB 300–500 per boat (negotiable, seats roughly 6–10 people). The ride out takes about 15 minutes. Two limestone peaks flank the river — soft late-afternoon light makes for great photos.

items.activity: Walk the riverside embankment in front of town (the black-crab plaza)
items.note: A riverside plaza in front of Chao Fah Pier with a cool breeze, where locals come to exercise. Stroll, catch the wind, and take in Khao Khanab Nam across the water for free.
In-town seafood restaurants are friendlier on price than the Ao Nang side. Order fresh prawns, crab, and squid — about THB 250–400 per person and you'll be full.

blocks.title: About the Khao Khanab Nam boat
blocks.html: Charter prices aren't fixed on any sign. Sort it out clearly with the boatman at Chao Fah Pier before you board — whether it includes landing on the islet, stopping for the cave walk, or just a loop. If you want to climb up and walk the cave, allow extra time and tell the driver in advance.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Nice-atmosphere cafes, closing out at the Walking Street

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Morning cafe, souvenirs, then eat your way through the Walking Street at night

items.activity: Breakfast — roti and tea in town
items.note: Krabi has a large Muslim community, and roti–pulled-tea shops open early. Banana-egg roti with hot tea is a light fill at about THB 40–60.

items.activity: Morning cafe at EP's Cafe Patisserie
items.note: An upscale-feeling cafe and patisserie that's actually affordable. Homemade bakery, good coffee, nice for a long sit and some photos.

items.activity: Lunch + a stop at Weasel Coffee (civet coffee)
items.note: An in-town coffee shop with several photo spots and both savory and sweet menus. Try the distinctive coffee as an experience — and if you don't drink coffee, there are other options.
Cashew nuts, shrimp-paste chili dip, and Khlong Thom shrimp paste — take your pick at the in-town souvenir shops, cheaper than buying at the airport.

items.activity: Back to the hotel, save energy for the evening
items.note: You've walked all day — head back to rest and shower, saving some energy for a long walk through the Walking Street tonight.

items.activity: Eat your way through Krabi Walking Street (Maharaj Road Soi 8, near Vogue mall)
items.note: Open Friday–Saturday–Sunday evenings, roughly 5:00–10:00 PM, with food, souvenirs, clothes, and a live-music stage in the middle of the street. Graze as you walk and dinner takes care of itself.

items.activity: End the trip with some live music
items.note: There are bars and seats along the Walking Street — grab a drink and listen to the band on the central stage. An easy way to close out the day.

items.name: Much Mellow
items.blurb: A minimalist wood-toned cafe in Soi Maharaj 2. The draw is its house-baked croissants and homemade bakery, with vegan options. Quiet enough to linger, with a hostel upstairs.

items.name: Urban café x workspace
items.blurb: A two-floor black-toned loft cafe in K-Avenue on Maharaj Road, right in town. Power outlets for working, good coffee, and plenty of drinks and cakes.
items.meta: K-Avenue, Maharaj Road · open 8:00 AM–6:00 PM

items.name: EP's Cafe Patisserie
items.blurb: An upscale-feeling cafe and patisserie that's genuinely affordable. Homemade bakery, good coffee, great for a relaxed sit, photos, and a light bite.

items.name: Weasel Coffee (civet coffee)
items.blurb: An in-town coffee shop with several photo spots, leading with a distinctive civet coffee. Both savory and sweet menus — worth trying as an experience.

blocks.html: All four are in or near the town center — reachable by motorbike taxi or on foot. If you want a cafe with a sea view or out in nature, you'll have to drive out toward Ao Nam Mao–Ao Nang, which strays a little from the "town" theme. Save that for a day you feel like heading out of town.

items: On foot — the Maharaj Road area, Chao Fah Pier, and the Walking Street are all within walking distance of each other, which suits this plan best
Motorbike taxi — easy to flag down in town and handy for cafes a bit further out
Renting a motorbike — about THB 200–300 a day, the most flexible if you want to hit several cafes
Taxi/Grab — available but not as dense as in big cities; for short in-town trips a motorbike taxi is faster

blocks.title: Pick a hotel that fits the theme
blocks.html: For a town-focused trip, stay in Krabi Town itself, not the Ao Nang side. You'll be within walking distance of the cafes, the Walking Street, and the pier, saving both money and time on transport.

faq.q: What days is Krabi Walking Street open?
faq.a: It opens only on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings, roughly 5:00–10:00 PM, on Maharaj Road Soi 8 near Vogue mall in central Krabi. Come on a weekday and you'll miss it, so plan your trip to line up a Walking Street night with a day you're in town.

faq.q: Where do you catch the boat to Khao Khanab Nam, and how much is it?
faq.a: Take a longtail boat from Chao Fah Pier in Krabi Town; it's about a 15-minute ride out. A round-trip charter runs roughly THB 300–500 per boat (negotiable, seats several people). There's no fixed-price sign, so agree clearly with the boatman before boarding.

faq.q: I'm in Krabi but don't want to do the islands — what is there to do?
faq.a: A town-focused trip works easily: stroll the Maharaj Road old town, sit in in-town cafes, take an evening boat to Khao Khanab Nam, and walk the Walking Street on the weekend. You can fill a full two days without ever heading out to sea.

faq.q: Are there cafes in Krabi Town where you can work?
faq.a: Yes — for example, Urban café x workspace at K-Avenue on Maharaj Road, a two-floor loft with power outlets, open 8:00 AM–6:00 PM, and Much Mellow in Soi Maharaj 2, which is quiet enough to settle in for a while.

faq.q: How many days should I spend in Krabi if I'm only doing the town?
faq.a: Two days and one night is just right. The first day focuses on cafes and Khao Khanab Nam; the second is a morning cafe, souvenir shopping, then the Walking Street in the evening. If you have more time, add an island trip or a day at Ao Nang.
